subject: Clarifying isolation expectations: Dedicated vs Private VPC
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Donnelly <jane.donnelly@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying isolation expectations: Dedicated vs Private VPC

Hi Jane — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap plus a short list of clarifying questions so we can size the right deployment option (Hosted API / Dedicated / Private VPC).

Call recap (high level)
- Use case: real-time transaction enrichment and PII redaction in customer-facing workflows.
- Volume: steady 200 reqs/minute with spikes to ~1k reqs/minute during batch runs.
- Latency target: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 400ms.

Key question for your security team: data isolation expectations. During the call you mentioned two potential directions — (A) Dedicated capacity with strict tenant isolation on Redwood-managed infra vs (B) Private VPC / on-prem where you control the network and keys. To make the next step efficient, could you confirm the following for each data class (PII, transaction metadata, model telemetry)?

1) Data residency: must all inference inputs/outputs remain in your VPC/region? (yes/no)
2) KMS requirement: do you require BYOK (customer-managed keys) / HSM integration or is Redwood-managed KMS acceptable? (BYOK / Redwood KMS)
3) Audit/logging: are full request-level audit logs required to live in your environment, or is streaming logs to your SIEM acceptable? (in-environment / forwarded)
4) Egress policy: is outbound model telemetry (anonymous metrics) blocked? (blocked / allowed)

If you prefer, we can send a short checkbox-based questionnaire that your GRC team can sign off on. I’ll attach a short comparison doc that highlights differences in isolation, operational responsibilities, and SLAs for Dedicated vs Private VPC.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm answers to 1–4 above (or attach the security questionnaire).
- If Private VPC is preferred, we route a technical scoping call with our infra partner to validate network & routing requirements.
- If Dedicated works, we prepare a sizing + SLA options sheet and a canary rollout plan.

Attaching the comparison doc now. Happy to jump on a quick 30-min follow-up with your infra/security leads this week.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0112

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-security-summary.pdf (summary of isolation controls / responsibilities)

From: Jane Donnelly <jane.donnelly@finservcorp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 16:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying isolation expectations: Dedicated vs Private VPC

Rishi — thanks for the summary and the doc. High-level responses below; I'm copying our security lead (cc'ed) in the questionnaire request internally.

Answers to your 4 questions (initial):
1) Data residency: YES — inference inputs/outputs with PII must remain in our controlled environment/region.
2) KMS requirement: BYOK required for PII. We will not accept provider-managed keys for sensitive data.
3) Audit/logging: In-environment audit logs preferred. We can accept forwarded logs only for non-PII telemetry.
4) Egress policy: outbound telemetry that contains request-level detail is blocked. Aggregated anonymous metrics ok.

A few clarifying items we need from Redwood to feed into procurement and architecture:
- Exact network egress ports and domains needed for Dedicated vs Private.
- Will Redwood Dedicated guarantee zero multi-tenant disk exposure (encryption + wiped between tenants)?
- For Private VPC, do you support customer-managed NAT/GW or require managed egress?

I'll attach a short GRC questionnaire (PDF) later today. If you can map the answers to each deployment option that would be ideal.

Regards,
Jane Donnelly
CISO (acting)
FinServ Corp

Forwarded attachment: finserv-data-isolation-qa.pdf (coming from FinServ GRC team)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Donnelly <jane.donnelly@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying isolation expectations: Dedicated vs Private VPC

Jane — thanks for the fast responses and for flagging the questionnaire. I’ve mapped your answers to the two deployment profiles below and attached a detailed checklist for your GRC team. Quick summary:

Option A — Redwood Dedicated (Redwood-managed infra, reserved GPU pools):
- Data residency: can be restricted to a single region; however data will traverse Redwood-managed control plane for orchestration by default. We offer an option to restrict control-plane metadata and to encrypt payloads end-to-end.
- KMS: supports customer BYOK via external KMS/HSM integration for encryption at rest. For strict BYOK-only mandates we provide a plan to rotate keys and segregate backup storage.
- Audit/logging: request/response logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. If in-environment log residency is required for PII, Dedicated requires a log-forwarding gateway with guaranteed TLS and signed delivery (we document retention/rotation).
- Egress: telemetry that contains request-level data can be disabled; only aggregated metrics will be emitted.
- Disk/Data wipe: Dedicated uses ephemeral volumes per tenant with NIST-152 style wipe procedures; we will document the wipe policy and retention windows.

Option B — Private VPC / On-prem (customer-managed infra):
- Data residency: all inference inputs/outputs remain inside your VPC/on-prem. Control plane calls are routed through a customer-controlled private endpoint.
- KMS: BYOK/HSM fully supported; keys never leave your key boundary.
- Audit/logging: full request-level audit logs can be stored in your environment; Redwood will ship binaries for local log ingestion or stream to your SIEM via private peering.
- Egress: zero outbound telemetry unless explicitly enabled.
- Operational scope: Redwood provides the inference runtime, orchestration layer can be run in a private control plane; customer owns patching for OS-level dependencies in on-prem setups (we offer an ops bundle).

Attached: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.xlsx — this is the checkbox-style questionnaire you can pass to GRC. I also attached a short technical note on required egress domains/ports and a sample network diagram.

Requested artifacts we can deliver this week for procurement/security review:
- SOC2 Type II summary and auditor letter
- Network egress / ports spreadsheet (with CIDR ranges)
- BYOK integration guide (KMS/HSM compatibility matrix)
- Wipe/retention policy excerpt for Dedicated deployments

Proposed next steps:
1) You share the completed GRC questionnaire (or confirm the answers above).
2) If Private VPC is required, we schedule a 60-min technical scoping with your infra and our infra-eng lead (I'll include Marissa).
3) If Dedicated is acceptable with BYOK + in-transit encryption + log-forwarding gateway, we'll prepare a dedicated capacity sizing + contract draft for review.

Let me know which path you prefer and any timing constraints for the scoping call.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.xlsx
Attachment: redwood-dedicated-security-summary.pdf
